text: After her husband died, Margaret Lowrie kept the light on the north headland for another twenty-six years. The lighthouse board paid her two-thirds of what it had paid him. Her logbooks for those years are the most complete the board ever received.
strengths: she is introduced by the job she did and how long she did it
her pay is measured against her husband's, so the listener feels it without hearing a sum
the pay and the logbooks are set side by side and the unfairness is never named
weaknesses: the two-thirds needs the board's pay records behind it
a film that closes every introduction on a quiet irony will start to sound arch
spokenRhythm: A long opening sentence carries the name, the job and the years, then two shorter sentences put the pay and the work next to each other.
narrativeFunction: Introduces a keeper by her work and lets the board's own records make the argument about how she was treated.
whyItWorks: The first thing the listener learns about Margaret Lowrie is what she did, so the name arrives attached to a job and a span of years. The next two sentences are plain facts from the same employer, and the gap between them does the work an adjective would have spoiled. Nobody is told to feel indignant, and most listeners will.

text: The canal company's surveyor was a schoolmaster named Daniel Ashby. He had taught himself surveying from a borrowed book, and his figures put the summit forty feet lower than it really was. The company found out when it started to dig.
strengths: the job comes before the name, and the name before anything else about him
the borrowed book explains the mistake without blaming him aloud
the last line lands the cost without a number
weaknesses: a listener will want to know what forty feet meant in locks and money, which the next lines must give
spokenRhythm: A short introduction, a longer sentence that carries the cause and the error, and a short dry close.
narrativeFunction: Introduces the man whose mistake the next part of the film will have to pay for.
whyItWorks: The listener learns who Ashby was and what he did in the order a person would tell it across a table. The error is stated as a measurement, and its consequence is left to one plain sentence that is funnier for not trying. It sets up the cost of the mistake without announcing that a cost is coming.

text: Tobias Wren assayed ore for the mining company, which meant that every claim on the hill was worth what he said it was worth. The company paid him a good salary. Several men in the town offered him a better one.
strengths: his job is explained by what it gave him power over
bribery is implied and never named
the last two sentences turn on a single word
weaknesses: the first sentence asks the listener to hold the job and its meaning at once
without a figure the listener can't judge how good the salary was
spokenRhythm: A long first sentence that explains the job, then two short ones that mirror each other and turn on one word.
narrativeFunction: Introduces the man at the centre of the corruption and plants the temptation before any accusation is made.
whyItWorks: It tells the listener why this person matters before it tells them anything about his character. The pairing of a good salary and a better one is dry, and it lets the audience reach the word bribery on their own. It is good rather than excellent because the opening sentence carries a lot for the ear.

text: Samuel Orme worked nights in the telegraph office at the junction. The message from the coast reached him a little after two in the morning. He sent it on at dawn. His statement to the inquiry runs to a single page, and it mentions the weather twice.
strengths: he is introduced by his post and his shift, and judged only by what he did
his state of mind is left to his own statement
the last line suggests an evasion without accusing him of one
weaknesses: dawn is vague, and the inquiry's own times should replace it if the film has them
the insinuation in the last clause needs the record of that night's weather behind it
spokenRhythm: A plain introduction, a medium sentence with the time, a five-word sentence for the delay, and a longer close that ends on its sting.
narrativeFunction: Introduces the operator whose delay the inquiry will examine, and raises the question of why without asking it.
whyItWorks: Nothing is said about what Orme thought or felt, because nothing survives to say it. The narration gives his job, his actions and the length of his excuse, in that order, and lets the detail about the weather do the doubting. The short third sentence makes the delay land as a fact before the listener is given any reason to judge it.

text: Most of what we know about Ruth Callow comes from the account books of the whaling agency she took over when her brother drowned. She fitted out eleven voyages. Seven came home with a profit. The entries are in her own hand, and she wrote up the losses as carefully as the gains.
strengths: the source is named in the same breath as the person
each number gets a sentence of its own, and the second is measured against the first
she is characterised by how she kept her books, not by an adjective
weaknesses: the opening sentence holds the name, the source, the business and a death
seven out of eleven means more once the film says how the port's other agencies fared
spokenRhythm: A long opening sentence, two short ones that carry one number each, and a longer close that turns from the figures to the woman who wrote them down.
narrativeFunction: Introduces a woman through the business records she left and lets the way she kept them stand for her character.
whyItWorks: It is honest about where the knowledge comes from, then gives her career in two numbers a listener can take one at a time. The close moves from what she achieved to how she recorded it, which says more about her than an adjective would, and it ends on information rather than a punchline. It is good rather than excellent because the first sentence carries too much.

text: The weavers' guild first took notice of Agnes Fell when it fined her for selling cloth without its seal. A week later it fined her again, for the same thing. Four years later it made her one of its wardens.
strengths: she enters the record, and the film, by breaking a rule
the payoff arrives as a plain fact
weaknesses: the echo of a week later and four years later is a device that works once in a sequence
over a whole film, ending each introduction on a reversal would become a formula
spokenRhythm: A long first sentence, then two shorter ones that echo each other's openings and step forward in time.
narrativeFunction: Introduces a character by her first appearance in the record and shows in one arc how she rose.
whyItWorks: Every sentence is an event, and together they draw a person without a single adjective about her. The guild's own decisions are the frame, so the narration claims nothing about her motives. The listener hears stubbornness and ability without being told either word.
